item.title: Saudi-led coalition claim more attacks on Houthis
item.description:
Saudi-led coalition claim more attacks on Houthis

The Saudi-led coalition said it carried out a military operation "aimed at neutralising sources of threat".

The coalition said it destroyed five tunnels used by the Houthis to store ballistic missiles, a missile depot and four platforms used to launch ballistic missiles.

It also claimed operations targeting Houthi "fortifications, gatherings of their members, and their military equipment along the front lines inside Yemen".

item.title: Report: Leading officials from Mecca pact to meet Iranian officials in Tehran
item.description:
Report: Leading officials from Mecca pact to meet Iranian officials in Tehran

Top officials from countries involved in the Mecca Pact are expected to meet Iranian officials in Tehran on Monday to discuss regional coordination, Reuters reported citing two sources. 

According to the sources, Saudi Arabia will be represented by Defence Minister Prince Khalid bin Salman, Pakistan by army chief Field Marshal Asim Munir as well as the Turkish head of intelligence.

item.title: Cabinet split emerges over controversial Rosebank oilfield decision
item.description:
Chancellor is in favour of North Sea project, but energy secretary has said she is leaning towards rejecting it

A cabinet split has emerged over whether to approve drilling at the Rosebank oilfield, with the chancellor, John Healey, in favour of the controversial North Sea project.

The energy secretary, Miatta Fahnbulleh, is ultimately in charge of the decision, and the Guardian reported last week that she was leaning towards rejecting it after granting permission for the smaller Jackdaw gasfield.

Joshua Loudermilk, one of two men apparently discredited by the new Ali G movie Ali G: Who Iz I?, has said that he was in on the joke, but that the film-makers didn’t realise this.

Loudermilk, a 54-year-old aspiring actor from North Carolina, has told the Guardian he recognised star Sacha Baron Cohen early in the shoot but continued pretending to be a hard-right Maga sympathiser prepared to defend the US border at all costs.

item.description: The Iran war has made oil tanker voyages so inefficient that vessel availability has crumbled and freight costs have soared to record-highs, all but erasing the incentive for shipping crude oil from the U.S. Gulf Coast to Asia. The cost of shipping crude oil from the U.S. Gulf Coast to China soared to as high as $80 million earlier this month. That’s ten times the average tanker rates that had held for years before the Iran war.
